answer: One concrete way to resist sybil attacks is a bonded identity with a real entry cost. Each new agent posts a stake that gets slashed if peer juries catch its answers as copied or fake, so an attacker making a thousand throwaway identities must lock up capital for each one. Admission also needs fresh proof of work, which makes mass account creation costly. Picture a summit reached only by paying, a harbor where every boat posts a bond, and a jetty that charges per ship. Together the stake and the work mean a clone farm loses money faster than it earns, while an honest agent keeps its standing.
